from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title_text = "Prerequisite: The Bernoulli Trial"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- A Bernoulli trial has exactly two outcomes.",
            "- We label success as p and failure as q.",
            "- Each dive Pixel takes is one independent trial."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Switch components
        switch_bg = RoundedRectangle(width=2.5, height=1.2, corner_radius=0.6, color=GRAY)
        self.place_in_area(switch_bg, "C3", "C4")
        
        switch_label = Text("Trial", font_size=24).next_to(switch_bg, UP, buff=0.3)
        
        success_text = Text("Success", color="#00FF00", font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(success_text, "C2")
        
        failure_text = Text("Failure", color="#FF0000", font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(failure_text, "C5")
        
        knob = Circle(radius=0.5, fill_opacity=1, color=WHITE)
        knob.move_to(switch_bg.get_left() + RIGHT * 0.6)
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(switch_bg), 
            FadeIn(switch_label), 
            FadeIn(success_text), 
            FadeIn(failure_text), 
            FadeIn(knob)
        )
        
        # Toggle animation: Success to Failure and back
        self.play(knob.animate.move_to(switch_bg.get_right() - RIGHT * 0.6), run_time=1)
        self.play(knob.animate.move_to(switch_bg.get_left() + RIGHT * 0.6), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        p_label = MathTex("p", color="#ADD8E6", font_size=48)
        self.place_at_grid(p_label, "B2")
        
        q_label = MathTex("q", color="#ADD8E6", font_size=48)
        self.place_at_grid(q_label, "B5")
        
        self.play(Write(p_label), Write(q_label))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create Pixel (simple penguin)
        body = Ellipse(width=0.8, height=1.2, fill_opacity=1, color=BLACK, stroke_color=WHITE)
        belly = Ellipse(width=0.5, height=0.8, fill_opacity=1, color=WHITE)
        belly.shift(DOWN*0.1)
        eye_l = Circle(radius=0.05, color=BLACK, fill_opacity=1).shift(UP*0.3 + LEFT*0.15)
        eye_r = Circle(radius=0.05, color=BLACK, fill_opacity=1).shift(UP*0.3 + RIGHT*0.15)
        beak = Triangle(color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=1).scale(0.1).rotate(PI).shift(UP*0.15)
        pixel = VGroup(body, belly, eye_l, eye_r, beak)
        
        self.place_at_grid(pixel, "E3")
        
        # Check and Cross
        check_mark = Text("✓", color="#00FF00", font_size=60)
        self.place_at_grid(check_mark, "E5")
        
        cross_mark = Text("✗", color="#FF0000", font_size=60)
        self.place_at_grid(cross_mark, "E5")

        self.play(FadeIn(pixel))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Dive 1 (Success)
        # Shift Pixel down-right to simulate a "dive"
        self.play(pixel.animate.shift(DOWN*0.5 + RIGHT*0.5), run_time=0.6)
        # Toggle switch to Success (left side)
        self.play(knob.animate.move_to(switch_bg.get_left() + RIGHT * 0.6), run_time=0.3)
        self.play(FadeIn(check_mark))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(check_mark), pixel.animate.move_to(self.grid["E3"]))
        
        # Dive 2 (Failure)
        self.play(pixel.animate.shift(DOWN*0.5 + RIGHT*0.5), run_time=0.6)
        # Toggle switch to Failure (right side)
        self.play(knob.animate.move_to(switch_bg.get_right() - RIGHT * 0.6), run_time=0.3)
        self.play(FadeIn(cross_mark))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(cross_mark), pixel.animate.move_to(self.grid["E3"]))
        
        self.wait(2)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "Defining the Binomial Distribution"
        lecture_lines = [
            "In a binomial distribution, we repeat several trials.",
            "We count the probability of exactly k successes.",
            "Tree diagrams show how possible outcomes branch out."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)
        
        color1 = "#33FF57"
        color2 = "#33C4FF"
        color3 = "#FF5733"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(color1))
        
        # Create 5 slots
        slots = VGroup(*[Rectangle(width=1.0, height=1.0, color=WHITE) for _ in range(5)])
        slots.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(slots, 'A1', 'A6')
        
        n_label = MathTex("n=5", color=color1)
        n_label.next_to(slots, UP)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(slots), Write(n_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(color2))
        
        success_color = "#00FF00"
        failure_color = "#FF0000"

        success_labels = VGroup()
        failure_labels = VGroup()

        # Highlight 3 slots as 'Success'
        success_indices = [0, 2, 4]
        for i in success_indices:
            slots[i].set_fill(success_color, opacity=0.5)
            label = Text("S", font_size=24, color=WHITE).move_to(slots[i].get_center())
            success_labels.add(label)

        # Highlight 2 slots as 'Failure'
        failure_indices = [1, 3]
        for i in failure_indices:
            slots[i].set_fill(failure_color, opacity=0.5)
            label = Text("F", font_size=24, color=WHITE).move_to(slots[i].get_center())
            failure_labels.add(label)
        
        k_label = MathTex("k=3", color=color2)
        k_label.next_to(slots, DOWN)

        self.play(
            LaggedStart(
                *[FadeIn(slots[i]) for i in success_indices],
                *[FadeIn(slots[i]) for i in failure_indices],
                lag_ratio=0.2
            ),
            Write(success_labels),
            Write(failure_labels),
            Write(k_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Prepare for next animation
        self.play(FadeOut(slots), FadeOut(n_label), FadeOut(k_label), FadeOut(success_labels), FadeOut(failure_labels))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(color3))
        
        # Create tree diagram
        root_pos = self.grid['C3']
        root = Dot(root_pos, color=WHITE)
        root_label = Text("Start", font_size=20).next_to(root, UP)
        self.play(FadeIn(root), Write(root_label))

        # Level 1
        level1_s_pos = root_pos + np.array([1, 1.5, 0])
        level1_f_pos = root_pos + np.array([1, -1.5, 0])
        level1_s = Dot(level1_s_pos, color=success_color)
        level1_f = Dot(level1_f_pos, color=failure_color)
        line1_s = Line(root.get_center(), level1_s.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        line1_f = Line(root.get_center(), level1_f.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        label1_s = MathTex("S", color=success_color).next_to(line1_s.get_center(), UP, buff=0.1)
        label1_f = MathTex("F", color=failure_color).next_to(line1_f.get_center(), DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(
            Create(line1_s), Create(line1_f),
            FadeIn(level1_s), FadeIn(level1_f),
            Write(label1_s), Write(label1_f)
        )

        # Level 2
        level2_ss_pos = level1_s_pos + np.array([1, 0.75, 0])
        level2_sf_pos = level1_s_pos + np.array([1, -0.75, 0])
        level2_fs_pos = level1_f_pos + np.array([1, 0.75, 0])
        level2_ff_pos = level1_f_pos + np.array([1, -0.75, 0])

        nodes_l2 = [Dot(pos, color=WHITE) for pos in [level2_ss_pos, level2_sf_pos, level2_fs_pos, level2_ff_pos]]
        nodes_l2[0].set_color(success_color)
        nodes_l2[1].set_color(failure_color)
        nodes_l2[2].set_color(success_color)
        nodes_l2[3].set_color(failure_color)
        
        lines_l2 = [
            Line(level1_s.get_center(), nodes_l2[0].get_center()),
            Line(level1_s.get_center(), nodes_l2[1].get_center()),
            Line(level1_f.get_center(), nodes_l2[2].get_center()),
            Line(level1_f.get_center(), nodes_l2[3].get_center())
        ]
        
        labels_l2 = [
            MathTex("S", color=success_color).next_to(lines_l2[0].get_center(), UP, buff=0.1),
            MathTex("F", color=failure_color).next_to(lines_l2[1].get_center(), DOWN, buff=0.1),
            MathTex("S", color=success_color).next_to(lines_l2[2].get_center(), UP, buff=0.1),
            MathTex("F", color=failure_color).next_to(lines_l2[3].get_center(), DOWN, buff=0.1)
        ]

        self.play(
            *[Create(line) for line in lines_l2],
            *[FadeIn(node) for node in nodes_l2],
            *[Write(label) for label in labels_l2]
        )
        
        # Level 3
        level3_positions = []
        for i in range(4):
            level3_positions.append(nodes_l2[i].get_center() + np.array([1, 0.375, 0]))
            level3_positions.append(nodes_l2[i].get_center() + np.array([1, -0.375, 0]))

        nodes_l3 = [Dot(pos, color=WHITE) for pos in level3_positions]
        for i in range(8):
            nodes_l3[i].set_color(success_color if i % 2 == 0 else failure_color)

        lines_l3 = [Line(nodes_l2[i//2].get_center(), nodes_l3[i].get_center()) for i in range(8)]
        
        labels_l3 = []
        for i, line in enumerate(lines_l3):
            label_text = "S" if i % 2 == 0 else "F"
            label_color = success_color if i % 2 == 0 else failure_color
            buff_dir = UP if i % 2 == 0 else DOWN
            labels_l3.append(MathTex(label_text, color=label_color).next_to(line.get_center(), buff_dir, buff=0.1))

        self.play(
            *[Create(line) for line in lines_l3],
            *[FadeIn(node) for node in nodes_l3],
            *[Write(label) for label in labels_l3]
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The 'BINS' Checklist"
        lines = [
            "Use the BINS acronym to check for binomial distributions.",
            "B stands for Binary: outcomes are success or failure.",
            "I means trials are independent of each other.",
            "N requires a fixed number of trials.",
            "S means the probability remains the same every time."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors for the BINS acronym
        color_b = "#00FFFF"  # Cyan
        color_i = "#FFFF00"  # Yellow
        color_n = "#00FF00"  # Green
        color_s = "#FFA500"  # Orange

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Use the BINS acronym to check for binomial distributions.
        
        b_txt = Text("B", font_size=72, color=color_b)
        i_txt = Text("I", font_size=72, color=color_i)
        n_txt = Text("N", font_size=72, color=color_n)
        s_txt = Text("S", font_size=72, color=color_s)
        
        bins_group = VGroup(b_txt, i_txt, n_txt, s_txt).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(bins_group, "A2", "B5")
        
        self.play(Write(bins_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # B stands for Binary: outcomes are success or failure.
        
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(color_b))
        
        # Highlight 'B' by making others dim
        self.play(
            i_txt.animate.set_opacity(0.3),
            n_txt.animate.set_opacity(0.3),
            s_txt.animate.set_opacity(0.3),
            b_txt.animate.scale(1.2)
        )
        
        # Binary toggle: Success / Failure
        s_label = Text("Success", font_size=24, color=GREEN)
        f_label = Text("Failure", font_size=24, color=RED)
        binary_vg = VGroup(s_label, f_label).arrange(RIGHT, buff=1)
        self.place_in_area(binary_vg, "C2", "C5")
        
        arrow = Arrow(UP, DOWN, color=WHITE).scale(0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(arrow, "D3") # Middle of Success/Failure area approx
        arrow.next_to(binary_vg, DOWN)

        self.play(Create(binary_vg))
        # Visual toggle effect
        self.play(s_label.animate.scale(1.2), f_label.animate.set_opacity(0.5), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(s_label.animate.scale(1/1.2).set_opacity(0.5), f_label.animate.scale(1.2).set_opacity(1), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(s_label.animate.set_opacity(1), f_label.animate.scale(1/1.2).set_opacity(1), run_time=0.5)
        
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(binary_vg), FadeOut(arrow))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # I means trials are independent of each other.
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(color_i),
            b_txt.animate.set_opacity(0.3).scale(1/1.2),
            i_txt.animate.set_opacity(1).scale(1.2)
        )
        
        # Two dice rolling independently
        def create_die(value):
            square = Square(side_length=0.8, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.1)
            dots = VGroup()
            if value == 1:
                dots.add(Dot(radius=0.05))
            elif value == 3:
                dots.add(Dot(radius=0.05).shift(UP*0.2+LEFT*0.2))
                dots.add(Dot(radius=0.05))
                dots.add(Dot(radius=0.05).shift(DOWN*0.2+RIGHT*0.2))
            elif value == 5:
                dots.add(Dot(radius=0.05).shift(UP*0.2+LEFT*0.2))
                dots.add(Dot(radius=0.05).shift(UP*0.2+RIGHT*0.2))
                dots.add(Dot(radius=0.05))
                dots.add(Dot(radius=0.05).shift(DOWN*0.2+LEFT*0.2))
                dots.add(Dot(radius=0.05).shift(DOWN*0.2+RIGHT*0.2))
            # ... simple enough for 2 dice
            return VGroup(square, dots)

        die1 = create_die(3)
        die2 = create_die(5)
        dice_vg = VGroup(die1, die2).arrange(RIGHT, buff=1)
        self.place_in_area(dice_vg, "C2", "C5")
        
        self.play(Create(dice_vg))
        # Roll them (rotate/change)
        self.play(
            Rotate(die1, angle=PI*2),
            Rotate(die2, angle=-PI*2),
            run_time=1
        )
        
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(dice_vg))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # N requires a fixed number of trials.
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(color_n),
            i_txt.animate.set_opacity(0.3).scale(1/1.2),
            n_txt.animate.set_opacity(1).scale(1.2)
        )
        
        # Counter hitting fixed limit n=5
        n_val = ValueTracker(0)
        n_label = always_redraw(lambda: 
            Text(f"n = {int(n_val.get_value())}", font_size=48, color=color_n)
        )
        self.place_in_area(n_label, "C2", "C5")
        
        target_n = Text("Target: n=5", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(target_n, "D3")
        
        self.play(Write(n_label), Write(target_n))
        self.play(n_val.animate.set_value(5), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(n_label), FadeOut(target_n))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # S means the probability remains the same every time.
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(color_s),
            n_txt.animate.set_opacity(0.3).scale(1/1.2),
            s_txt.animate.set_opacity(1).scale(1.2)
        )
        
        # Probability value fixed at 0.6
        p_label = Text("p = 0.6", font_size=48, color=color_s)
        self.place_in_area(p_label, "C2", "C5")
        
        consistency_txt = Text("Constant", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(consistency_txt, "D3")
        
        self.play(Write(p_label), Write(consistency_txt))
        
        # Show it staying same while other things might change (not really needed but for emphasis)
        self.play(p_label.animate.scale(1.1), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(p_label.animate.scale(1/1.1), run_time=0.5)
        
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Reset acronym to full visibility
        self.play(
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            b_txt.animate.set_opacity(1),
            i_txt.animate.set_opacity(1),
            n_txt.animate.set_opacity(1),
            s_txt.animate.scale(1/1.2),
            FadeOut(p_label),
            FadeOut(consistency_txt)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data
        title = "The Shape of Probability"
        lines = [
            "- Histograms visualize the probability of each success count.",
            "- Changing the probability p shifts the distribution's center.",
            "- Increasing the trial count n creates a bell shape."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_L1 = "#FFFF00"  # Yellow
        COLOR_L2 = "#00FFFF"  # Cyan
        COLOR_L3 = "#00FF00"  # Green
        AXES_COLOR = "#D3D3D3"
        
        # State trackers
        p_val = ValueTracker(0.3)
        n_val = ValueTracker(5)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Color matching line 1
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_L1)
        
        # Create Axes for histogram
        # x_range covers max n=20. y_range covers max prob (~0.6 for small n, p)
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 21, 5],
            y_range=[0, 0.6, 0.2],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"color": AXES_COLOR, "include_tip": False},
            tips=False
        )
        # Positioning in 6x6 grid area
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B1", "F6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        k_label = Text("k (Successes)", font_size=16, color=AXES_COLOR)
        pk_label = Text("P(k)", font_size=16, color=AXES_COLOR)
        k_label.next_to(axes.x_axis, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        pk_label.next_to(axes.y_axis, LEFT, buff=0.2)
        
        # Pre-create bars (21 for max n=20) to maintain persistence
        bars = VGroup()
        for k in range(21):
            bar = Rectangle(
                width=axes.x_axis.get_unit_size() * 0.8,
                height=0.01,
                fill_opacity=0.7,
                fill_color=COLOR_L1,
                stroke_width=1,
                stroke_color=WHITE
            )
            bar.move_to(axes.c2p(k, 0), aligned_edge=DOWN)
            bars.add(bar)
            
        def update_bars(m):
            n_curr = int(n_val.get_value())
            p_curr = p_val.get_value()
            unit_h = axes.y_axis.get_unit_size()
            # Inherit color from the group to allow color changes during scene
            current_color = m.get_color()
            for k, bar in enumerate(m):
                if k <= n_curr:
                    # Binomial Probability calculation: P(k) = C(n,k) * p^k * (1-p)^(n-k)
                    try:
                        prob = math.comb(n_curr, k) * (p_curr**k) * ((1-p_curr)**(n_curr-k))
                    except (ValueError, OverflowError):
                        prob = 0
                    
                    new_height = max(unit_h * prob, 0.05) # Minimum height for visibility
                    bar.stretch_to_fit_height(new_height, about_edge=DOWN)
                    bar.move_to(axes.c2p(k, 0), aligned_edge=DOWN)
                    bar.set_fill(color=current_color, opacity=0.7)
                    bar.set_stroke(opacity=1)
                else:
                    # Hide bars for k > n
                    bar.set_fill(opacity=0)
                    bar.set_stroke(opacity=0)

        # Initialize bars state
        update_bars(bars)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), Write(k_label), Write(pk_label))
        self.play(FadeIn(bars))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_L2)
        bars.set_color(COLOR_L2) # Transition bar color to match next lecture line
        
        # Controls readouts
        p_label_text = Text("p = ", font_size=20, color=COLOR_L2)
        p_num = DecimalNumber(p_val.get_value(), num_decimal_places=2, color=COLOR_L2, font_size=20)
        p_group = VGroup(p_label_text, p_num).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        n_label_text = Text("n = ", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        n_num = DecimalNumber(n_val.get_value(), num_decimal_places=0, color=WHITE, font_size=20)
        n_group = VGroup(n_label_text, n_num).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        controls = VGroup(p_group, n_group).arrange(RIGHT, buff=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(controls, "A3")
        
        # Updaters for real-time changes
        p_num.add_updater(lambda d: d.set_value(p_val.get_value()))
        bars.add_updater(update_bars)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(controls))
        # Animate p slider behavior
        self.play(p_val.animate.set_value(0.9), run_time=2.5, rate_func=linear)
        self.play(p_val.animate.set_value(0.1), run_time=2.5, rate_func=linear)
        self.play(p_val.animate.set_value(0.5), run_time=1.5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_L3)
        bars.set_color(COLOR_L3) # Transition bar color
        
        # Highlight n readout
        n_label_text.set_color(COLOR_L3)
        n_num.set_color(COLOR_L3)
        
        n_num.add_updater(lambda d: d.set_value(n_val.get_value()))
        
        # Animate n increasing to show smoothing effect
        self.play(n_val.animate.set_value(20), run_time=5, rate_func=smooth)
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Final cleanup
        bars.remove_updater(update_bars)
        p_num.remove_updater(None)
        n_num.remove_updater(None)

        ]
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Application & Summary", lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        robot = VGroup(robot_body, robot_eye_l, robot_eye_r)
        self.place_at_grid(robot, "C3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Scanning beam
        beam = Polygon(self.grid["C3"], self.grid["E3"] + LEFT*0.25, self.grid["E3"] + RIGHT*0.25, 
                       color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_width=0)
        
        self.add(conveyor, robot)
        
        results = ["#00FF00", "#FF0000", "#00FF00"]
        labels = ["Pass", "Fail", "Pass"]
        
        items = []
        for i in range(3):
            item = Square(side_length=0.4, fill_opacity=1, color=GREY_B)

outline.topic: Binomial Distributions: The Math of Success and Failure
outline.target_audience: High school or introductory college students

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Bernoulli Trial
sections.content: Introduce the foundation of binomial distributions: the Bernoulli trial. Explain that it is a single event with exactly two outcomes: Success (p) or Failure (q). Visually represent this as a single 'on/off' switch.
sections.example: Meet 'Pixel the Penguin' who is trying to catch a fish. Each dive is a Bernoulli trial: either he catches one (Success) or he doesn't (Failure).

sections.title: Defining the Binomial Distribution
sections.content: Transition from one trial to many. Define the Binomial Distribution as the probability of getting exactly 'k' successes in 'n' independent trials. Use a tree diagram animation to show how paths multiply as trials increase.
sections.example: If Pixel dives 5 times (n=5), what are the chances he catches exactly 3 fish (k=3)?

sections.title: The 'BINS' Checklist
sections.content: Introduce the four mandatory conditions for a distribution to be Binomial using the BINS acronym. 1. Binary (Success/Failure), 2. Independent (one trial doesn't affect the next), 3. Number (fixed number of trials), 4. Same probability (p remains constant).
sections.example: An animated checklist appears over Pixel's fishing trips to verify: 1. Catch/No catch? Yes. 2. Dives independent? Yes. 3. Exactly 5 dives? Yes. 4. Skill stays same (p=0.6)? Yes.

sections.title: Visualizing the Formula
sections.content: Break down the formula P(X=k) = nCk * p^k * q^(n-k). Use color-coding: nCk (The number of ways to arrange successes), p^k (The probability of successes), and q^(n-k) (The probability of failures). Show these as building blocks that fit together.
sections.example: Highlighting why we use '5 choose 3': It represents the different sequences of dives where Pixel could have caught 3 fish (e.g., Success-Success-Success-Fail-Fail vs. Fail-Fail-Success-Success-Success).

sections.title: The Shape of Probability
sections.content: Demonstrate how the distribution looks graphically. Use a histogram where the x-axis is the number of successes (k) and the y-axis is the probability. Show how the graph shifts from 'skewed' to 'bell-shaped' as 'n' increases or 'p' approaches 0.5.
sections.example: An animated bar chart shows Pixel's likelihood of catching 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5 fish. As his skill (p) improves, the highest bar moves from the left to the right side of the chart.

sections.title: Real-World Application & Summary
sections.content: Summarize the key takeaways: BINS criteria and the power of predicting outcomes in repeated trials. Briefly mention applications like quality control in factories or drug testing.
sections.example: Show a factory robot 'Box-Bot' checking 100 circuit boards. If the defect rate is 2%, the Binomial Distribution helps the factory predict how many failures to expect in a batch.
